flashcard_questions.q: Which ironic subtitle did Orwell give Animal Farm?

flashcard_questions.a: A story with a hidden political or moral meaning.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Russian ruler does Mr Jones represent?
Which Soviet dictator does Napoleon represent?
Which exiled revolutionary does Snowball represent?
What does Squealer represent in the allegory?
flashcard_questions.a: Soviet propaganda, especially the state newspaper Pravda.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the Russian word Pravda mean?
Which class does Boxer represent in the allegory?
Which secret police force do Napoleon’s dogs stand for?
When did Russia have its two revolutions?
Who led the Bolsheviks when they seized power in October?
When did Stalin take control of the Soviet Union?

flashcard_questions.a: The use of humour or exaggeration to criticise or ridicule politics and society.

flashcard_questions.q: Which two words were added to the bed commandment to excuse the pigs?
Which political position did Orwell himself hold?

notes: 15 cards: 6 allegory mappings (Jones, Napoleon, Snowball, Squealer, Boxer, the dogs), 3 context dates or people (1917, Lenin, 1924), 3 term-to-definition (allegory, satire, Pravda), 2 text-detail cards (the subtitle, ‘with sheets’), 1 author-position card (democratic socialist). ‘Fable’, ‘anthropomorphism’, ‘totalitarianism’ and ‘proletariat’ dropped — four abstract definitions in one deck would interfere badly with allegory and satire, which are the two the exam actually rewards. Aesop and the 1945 publication date trimmed to stay within 15.
